name: Mattithiah
overview: Mattithiah was a male Levite, specifically the son of Jeduthun, who was set apart to prophesy with musical instruments including lyres, harps, and cymbals. He was chosen as the fourteenth by lot among the singers, indicating a special role within the Levitical musicians. His ministry involved worship through music, reflecting the sacred duties assigned to the tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattithiah means 'gift of YHWH,' highlighting the divine blessing implied in his identity. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:3, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but reflects the theistic meaning common in Hebrew names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mattithiah as the son of Jeduthun, a detail that situates him within a prominent Levitical family known for musical service. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Mattithiah's significance lies in his role within the Levitical singers who were dedicated to prophesying through music, a ministry that combined worship and divine revelation. Being the fourteenth chosen by lot among the singers underscores the organized and divinely guided nature of temple worship. His service exemplifies the biblical principle that musical worship was a vital part of Israel's spiritual life, particularly among the tribe of Levi.
